Give reasons: Deliquescent substances tum into liquid when exposed to atmospheric air.

Deliquescent substances are the substances which can absorb such a huge amount of moisture fronm the air when exposed to atmospheric air and they dissolve in it to become a liquid. Deliquescence occurs when the vapour pressure of the solution that is formed is less than the partial pressure Of water vapour in the air.
Give reasons: Efflorescent substances lose water of crystallization after being exposed to air.

Efflorescent substances lose water of crystallization after being exposed to Qir, when the aqueous vapour pressure of hydrated salt is greater than that of the partial pressure of the water vapour in the air. Example: vapour pressure of washing soda (Na2C03.10H20) is normally exceed than that of water vapour in the-atmosphere.
